newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina beats IMF goal with $1.31 bln H1 deficit.
newsitem.headline: Argentina beats IMF goal with $1.31 bln H1 deficit.

text.p: Argentina reported Monday a first-half fiscal deficit of $1.31 billion, meaning it beat the first-half deficit target of $1.4 billion agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
"This surpasses our preliminary estimates," said Treasury Secretary Pablo Guidotti, announcing the figures to reporters.
The first-half deficit compares with a shortfall of $2.51 in the same period of 1996.
The June deficit was $73.1 million, compared with deficits of $127.5 million in May and $51 million in June last year.

Argentina had agreed with the IMF a deficit goal of about $3.0 billion this year -- $1.4 billion in the first half of the year, $600 million in the third quarter and $1.0 billion in the final quarter.

"We got more than we expected because of an increase in revenues from the fiscal package of last September and the improvement in economic activity, as well as tighter control on spending," said Guidotti.

Guidotti had previewed the fiscal result in an interview with Ambito Financiero newspaper published Monday, in which he said that the second-half goals were "equally hard to reach and they will also be met."
